method: Evidence-based adjudication of three blind primary proposals; agreement was treated as evidence rather than authority.

route.title: Word-event superscription
route.deciding_seam: The word-event, genealogy, and date notice closes before first-person sweeping judgment speech begins at Zeph.1.2.
route.defensible_basis: The notice has a distinct framing function and the speech beginning at 1:2 has its own repeated sweeping register.
route.counterevidence: The superscription governs the whole book and therefore still requires book-level context.

route.title: Programmatic sweeping judgment
route.deciding_seam: Repeated sweeping verbs expand across humans and creatures and close with a speech formula before the geographic narrowing to Judah and Jerusalem at Zeph.1.4.
rejected_alternatives: Separate chunks for members of the creature register
route.defensible_basis: The global scope and cumulative creature register form a compact programmatic oracle whose scope changes materially at 1:4.
route.counterevidence: Cutting-off language continues into 1:4, but the geographic and object narrowing is the stronger surface seam.

route.title: Judah and Jerusalem cultic indictment
route.deciding_seam: The hand-against-Judah-and-Jerusalem declaration introduces coordinated cultic allegiance, withdrawal, and failure-to-seek accusations; the hush imperative restarts the discourse at Zeph.1.7.
route.defensible_basis: The coordinated indictment has one geographic scope and rhetorical function and resolves before the new hush-and-sacrifice tableau.
route.counterevidence: The catalogue moves from named practices to the broader failure to seek, creating internal variation but not a stronger surface boundary.

route.title: Hush, sacrifice, and punishment tableau
route.deciding_seam: The hush command and near-day declaration develop through prepared sacrifice and punishment; a WLC-family samekh follows Zeph.1.9 before the city soundscape begins at 1:10.
route.defensible_basis: Imperative, sacrifice imagery, punishment catalogue, and paragraph evidence converge on a coherent local tableau.
route.counterevidence: Day language continues throughout 1:10-18, requiring the larger day-complex parent.

route.title: Jerusalem soundscape and lamp search
route.deciding_seam: The in-that-day city soundscape moves through merchant lament and lamp search to the complacency saying and property reversal; the great-day refrain restarts at Zeph.1.14.
route.defensible_basis: Public cries, commercial collapse, private search, quoted complacency, and reversal comprise one citywide judgment movement.
route.counterevidence: The move from public soundscape to private lamp search at 1:12 is a recoverable internal turn.

route.title: The great day poem
route.deciding_seam: The great-day restart and repeated day register escalate through battle, darkness, alarm, distress, blood, fire, and terminal closure; a WLC-family samekh follows Zeph.1.18.
route.defensible_basis: The repeated day descriptors and escalating consequences form a complete poetic movement with marked closure.
route.counterevidence: The consequences in 1:17-18 could be treated as a dependent concluding stanza.

route.title: Gather and seek appeal
route.deciding_seam: Repeated gathering, before, and seek expressions culminate in possible concealment; the causal nations rationale begins at Zeph.2.4.
route.defensible_basis: The imperatives and temporal urgency form a complete communal appeal and prevent 2:3 from surfacing as generic advice.
route.counterevidence: The terse wording and addressee scope of 2:1 remain translation-sensitive without changing the surface boundary.

route.title: Philistine coast oracle and remnant reversal
route.deciding_seam: The causal four-city catalogue at Zeph.2.4 prepares the coast woe, desolation, and Judah-remnant reversal through 2:7; Zeph.2.8 begins a new first-person hearing oracle concerning Moab and Ammon.
route.defensible_basis: Causal continuity and the coastland movement from city loss through desolation to remnant reversal outweigh the paragraph pressure to expose Zeph.2.4 independently.
route.counterevidence: The WLC-family samekh after 2:4 and fresh woe at 2:5 support a real dependent child seam; that seam is preserved as dissent rather than erased.

route.title: Moab and Ammon reproach and reversal
route.deciding_seam: First-person hearing, oath, Sodom-and-Gomorrah comparison, remnant inheritance, pride rationale, and widened worship horizon form one oracle before the direct Cush address at Zeph.2.12.
route.defensible_basis: The widening horizon in 2:11 is the rhetorical result of the named-nations oracle rather than an unrelated maxim.
route.counterevidence: Zeph.2.11 broadens beyond Moab and Ammon and could be retained as a dependent concluding horizon child.

route.title: Brief Cush oracle
route.deciding_seam: The second-person Cush address and complete sword clause create a compact compass-cycle turn; the northward Assyria movement begins at Zeph.2.13.
route.defensible_basis: Distinct direct address, named addressee, complete clause, and the geographic shift at 2:13 justify a one-verse literary unit.
route.counterevidence: Its brevity makes isolated retrieval risky; it must retain nations-cycle hydration and cannot authorize historical or ethnic conclusions.

route.title: Nineveh desolation and taunt
route.deciding_seam: The northern turn, desolation, animal habitation, exposed architecture, proud self-speech, and passerby response close together before the WLC-family samekh after Zeph.2.15.
route.defensible_basis: Desolation tableau and proud-city taunt are accusation and outcome within one named northern-city oracle.
route.counterevidence: The city self-speech at 2:15 is a strong internal rhetorical turn.

route.title: Rebellious city woe
route.deciding_seam: The city woe, four failures, predatory leaders, treacherous prophets, profaning priests, and righteous-Yahweh contrast form one movement before the destroyed-nations example at Zeph.3.6.
route.defensible_basis: The divine contrast in 3:5 answers the preceding leadership and cult indictment and belongs with it.
route.counterevidence: Zeph.3.5 changes from accusation to divine contrast and remains a recoverable dependent turn.

route.title: Warning example and failed correction
route.deciding_seam: The destroyed-nations example leads to the quoted correction summons and failed response; therefore-wait-for-me pivots at Zeph.3.8.
rejected_alternatives: Separate the correction quotation from its failed response
route.defensible_basis: Example, expected correction, and failed response form a complete warning-response movement before the inferential pivot.
route.counterevidence: Pronoun and causal scope link the movement backward to the city woe and forward to the therefore clause.

route.title: Judicial wait and assembly pivot
route.deciding_seam: Therefore-wait-for-me gathers the preceding failed correction into a judicial assembly declaration; the for-then expression at Zeph.3.9 turns from judgment to purified speech and service.
route.defensible_basis: Its inferential opening, wait summons, assembly language, and judgment culmination make it a recoverable pivot, while the causal-temporal turn at 3:9 begins the resulting promise movement.
route.counterevidence: The verse depends strongly on both neighboring movements and must never surface without the Zeph.3.8-Zeph.3.13 parent.

route.title: Purified peoples and dispersed worshipers
route.deciding_seam: The for-then turn develops purified speech, joint service, and dispersed worshipers through Zeph.3.10; the in-that-day formula and renewed feminine-singular city address begin a distinct remnant movement at 3:11.
route.defensible_basis: The causal-temporal opening, peoples-oriented purification and service, and dispersed-worshiper continuation form a dependent promise child; the temporal and address reset at 3:11 is strong enough to expose the next child separately.
route.counterevidence: Purification, pride removal, and remnant formation remain one larger restoration sequence, so the canonical lane's whole Zeph.3.9-Zeph.3.13 surface remains a defensible dissent.

route.title: Humble and secure remnant
route.deciding_seam: The in-that-day formula and city address introduce removal of pride and the remaining humble people; truthful speech, rest, and safety close before the WLC-family samekh after Zeph.3.13.
route.defensible_basis: Temporal and address reset, remnant focus, coordinated character-and-security description, and marked closure converge on this child unit.
route.counterevidence: The unit is causally continuous with purification in 3:9-10 and cannot be treated as an independent identity proposition.

route.title: Zion song and divine rejoicing
route.deciding_seam: Song imperatives at Zeph.3.14 develop through removed judgments, royal presence, the fear-not reassurance reported at 3:16, saving presence, and divine rejoicing through 3:17.
route.defensible_basis: The reported reassurance at 3:16 develops the song's grounds for rejoicing rather than starting a new oracle; royal and saving presence unites 3:15-17.
route.counterevidence: The in-that-day report at 3:16 is a genuine internal speech seam and supports the canonical lane's proposed child division.

route.title: Closing restoration and return
route.deciding_seam: The difficult first-person collection language at Zeph.3.18 proceeds into explicit rescue, gathering, praise, and return language and closes with the says-Yahweh formula at 3:20.
rejected_alternatives: Detach Zeph.3.20 as an isolated promise
route.defensible_basis: First-person collection, rescue, gathering, praise, return, and the terminal speech formula support a closing restoration movement while avoiding a preferred resolution of Zeph.3.18's syntax.
route.counterevidence: The syntax and subject scope of Zeph.3.18 are difficult and may connect backward to the song or its festal setting; this lowers confidence but does not presently require a boundary hold.

contested_case_rulings.ruling: Keep Zeph.2.4-Zeph.2.7 as the surface unit and preserve Zeph.2.4 plus Zeph.2.5-Zeph.2.7 as a dependent-child dissent.
contested_case_rulings.reason: The samekh and fresh woe are real seam evidence, but the causal city catalogue prepares the coast judgment and remnant reversal. Larger-unit continuity is stronger for surface retrieval.

contested_case_rulings.ruling: Surface Zeph.2.12 as a one-verse direct-address oracle with mandatory Zeph.2.4-Zeph.2.15 hydration.
contested_case_rulings.reason: A distinct addressee, complete sword clause, and northward change at 2:13 establish a recoverable compass-cycle child; brevity is managed through parent hydration.

contested_case_rulings.ruling: Surface Zeph.3.8 as a one-verse pivot with mandatory Zeph.3.8-Zeph.3.13 hydration.
contested_case_rulings.reason: Therefore-wait-for-me concludes the failed-correction sequence through assembly and judgment, while for-then at 3:9 starts the resulting purification movement. Dependency on both sides lowers confidence but does not erase the pivot.

contested_case_rulings.case: Whole Zeph.3.9-Zeph.3.13 versus Zeph.3.9-3.10 and Zeph.3.11-3.13
contested_case_rulings.ruling: Select the split Zeph.3.9-Zeph.3.10 and Zeph.3.11-Zeph.3.13 route, with Zeph.3.8-Zeph.3.13 mandatory for both children.
contested_case_rulings.reason: Zeph.3.9 begins a for-then purification and shared-service movement continued by dispersed worshipers in 3:10. Zeph.3.11 resets with in-that-day and renewed city address, then develops pride removal and the humble remnant through the samekh after 3:13. These are two distinct but dependent promise movements. This ruling rests on form, temporal reset, address shift, and closure rather than the number of supporting lanes.

contested_case_rulings.ruling: Keep Zeph.3.14-Zeph.3.17 whole and preserve Zeph.3.14-3.15 plus Zeph.3.16-3.17 as a child-seam dissent.
contested_case_rulings.reason: The reassurance reported at 3:16 supplies grounds for the song's rejoicing, and royal/saving presence connects 3:15-17. The speech turn is genuine but subordinate to the whole song-reassurance movement.

contested_case_rulings.ruling: Keep Zeph.3.18-Zeph.3.20 as the closing restoration oracle.
contested_case_rulings.reason: Despite unresolved syntax and subject scope, first-person collection leads coherently into rescue, gathering, praise, return, and the final speech formula. Backward attachment remains counterevidence and lowers confidence.

preserved_dissents.evidence: WLC-family samekh after Zeph.2.4 and the fresh coastland woe at 2:5.
preserved_dissents.boss_treatment: Preserved as a dependent child seam; not selected for the surface route.

preserved_dissents.alternative: Keep Zeph.3.8-Zeph.3.13 whole rather than surfacing the pivot child.
preserved_dissents.evidence: The judicial pivot depends on the purification and remnant outcomes that follow.
preserved_dissents.boss_treatment: Preserved; Zeph.3.8 may surface only with mandatory Zeph.3.8-Zeph.3.13 hydration.

preserved_dissents.evidence: Purification, shared service, pride removal, and remnant formation form one causal restoration sequence.
preserved_dissents.boss_treatment: Preserved as the principal losing alternative; split children selected because the 3:11 temporal/address reset and 3:13 closure are stronger local seam evidence.

preserved_dissents.evidence: The in-that-day reported reassurance at Zeph.3.16 is a real internal speech turn.
preserved_dissents.boss_treatment: Preserved as a child seam; whole song-and-reassurance surface selected.

preserved_dissents.alternative: Attach Zeph.3.18 backward to the Zion song.
preserved_dissents.evidence: Zeph.3.18 has difficult syntax and subject scope and may relate backward to the song or festal setting.
preserved_dissents.boss_treatment: Preserved as counterevidence; Zeph.3.18-Zeph.3.20 selected at medium confidence without deciding translation.

source_gaps: No authorized passage-pinned primary LXX, DSS, Targum, rabbinic, Second-Temple, or ANE evidence was available.
OSHB and UXLC are correlated WLC-family views and are not independent textual votes.
The terse wording of Zeph.2.1 remains unresolved but does not alter the selected boundary.
The syntax and subject scope of Zeph.3.18 remain unresolved; no preferred English translation or Hebrew construal is authorized.
hold_assessment: No primary proposed a boundary-affecting hold, and each contested seam can be selected on literary evidence while preserving the losing alternative and mandatory parent hydration. The unresolved Zeph.3.18 translation question lowers confidence but is not presently an answerable surface-boundary dispute requiring human or external-AI deferral.
